chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ullah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I performed Tamattu', slaughtered [the sacrificial animal], and shaved [my head]. Should I apply henna to my head? He said: Yes, provided you do not touch anything of the perfume. I said: Should I wear the shirt? He said: Yes, if you wish. I said: Should I cover my head? He said: Yes.

key_terms.تَمَتَّعْتُ: I performed Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is permissible after shaving the head during Hajj before Tawaf al-Ziyarah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfabar highlights the gradual transition from the state of Ihram to full permissibility (Hal) for a Mutamatti' pilgrim after shaving, specifically addressing the application of henna and wearing the shirt. It underscores the scholarly distinction that while most restrictions lift, the prohibition on using perfume (Tayyib) remains until the completion of Tawaf al-Ziyarah, reflecting the careful legal nuances in Shia fiqh regarding ritual purity and adornment during Hajj.
